sermon.title: Beasts, Saints, and Harvests Part 2
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In this second lesson on the beasts of Revelation 13, Pastor David G. Kincer says those written in the Book of Life will not worship the beast, and that the saints are still here, not raptured out. He explains the second beast’s false wonders and speaking idol, questions three-and-a-half-year charts and date-setting, offers his own explanation of 666, and teaches that sorcerers and false signs have only limited power.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: he cites “Acts 88:9” (caption), which is Acts 8:9, and “Revelation 1 and Revelation 226,” which is Revelation 1:1 and 22:6. Other passages (Revelation 13:8 and 14:12, John 3:5, Acts 17:24, Psalm 115, Deuteronomy 13:1–3, Exodus 7–8, 2 Corinthians 11:14–15, 2 Peter 3:8, Matthew 24:36 and 25) are given by his wording rather than a spoken reference and are linked to the matching passages; where he reads Scripture aloud his wording often differs from the NKJV text shown. In this message he names two recent national political leaders (about 3:07), compares his own explanation of 666 with theories about historical figures (about 13:33), refers to a revival in Lakeland, Florida (about 17:21), an Alabama revival meeting where he describes a person as having a familiar spirit (about 20:55), a prophet-test remark that names his wife (about 22:57), a “temple of Omar” and “a certain Jewish sect” (about 6:40), and images of other religions (about 5:41); he also comments on welfare and health programs. These are his own opinions and accounts, have not been checked by this site, and are kept out of the short answers; names appear in the transcript only. “[Unclear]” marks five spots where the captions were not clear (about 0:12, 3:24, 6:59, 17:25 and 19:55).

chunks.section_question: Who does not worship the beast? (Revelation 13:8, 14:12)
chunks.short_answer: He says “all worship the beast and Satan, except some people,” “those in the Book of Life,” the ones “that got born again.” He says they “didn’t join a church” or get a baptismal certificate; they “were touched by God.” He says churches “just put people on the roll book,” Jesus said “you got to be born again of the word and the Spirit,” and the saints’ faith is “in Jesus Christ, not in a church, not in a person, not in a minister.”
chunks.text:
All worship the beast and Satan, except some people. And who are these people? [unclear]. Guess what that is? It’s not bacon and lettuce. Those in the Book of Life. Those in the Book of Life won’t worship the natural people who are expressing the kingdom of darkness, and they won’t worship the king of the kingdom of darkness. They won’t do it. Can I hear an amen? Amen. See, all the earth worships, but the ones written in the Book of Life, the ones that got born again, the ones that really got the real deal when they came to Christ, they didn’t join a church, they didn’t get a baptismal certificate and, and go through a ritual. They were touched by God, they responded to God, they got birthed by God, and they follow him.

Amen. Churches just put people on the roll book, they just want attendance. You come, okay, we’ll put you on the roll book. He’s saved? How? No. Jesus said you got to be born again of the word and the Spirit. Of what? The word and the Spirit. And how are they going to get birthed in the word if we don’t preach the word? Are you with me? Hallelujah. And it says, “This is the patience and the faith of the saints.” Why? They’re going to stick with Jesus no matter what. These people are patient, they know God is going to fulfill his will. These people have their faith in Jesus Christ, not in a church, not in a person, not in a minister. Their faith is in Jesus Christ, and they are patiently waiting for Jesus to fulfill his word in them and in the world.

chunks.section_question: Are the saints raptured out, or kept through difficulty?
chunks.short_answer: Asked whether these saints are raptured, he says “No, they’re still here.” He says “Jesus is big enough to keep us in any kind of difficulty of this world” and “we don’t have to get raptured out.”
chunks.text: Hallelujah. Powerful, isn’t it? And where are they at? Are they raptured? No, they’re still here. I’ve showed you last week and the week before, they’re still here. These people are still here. Let me know, Jesus is big enough to keep us in any kind of difficulty of this world. We don’t have to get raptured out. We’re not that weak. Some of us are weak, we want to be raptured out.

chunks.section_question: What does he say is the difference between a believer and a Christian? (Revelation 13:11)
chunks.short_answer: He says the second beast “has all the power of the first beast,” including “the ability to speak,” and compares that to two recent national leaders he says “claimed to be Christians, and they lied to us.” He says “Christian means I came from Christ, I follow Christ, I act like Christ,” that “believer’s a stage,” and “just move on down the line” to maturity: “stick with the King.”
chunks.text:
Now, a second beast comes up, and the second beast has all the power of the first beast. So he’s got the ability to speak. That’s what the first beast had, the power to speak. Obama has great speaking abilities. Bush had great speaking abilities. I use them both because one was a Republican, one was a Democrat, both of them claimed to be Christians, and they lied to us. What does the word Christian mean? Yes. [unclear] means from or like, you know, a, a mannerism. Ephesians means what? You come from Ephesus. Yes. Christian means I came from Christ, I follow Christ, I act like Christ. See, there’s a big difference between a believer and a Christian. And believer’s a stage, don’t get me wrong, there’s nothing wrong, we got to go through the stages, am I right? Yeah. We got to believe, you know, we got to follow and all that. There’s nothing wrong if you’re a believer today, it’s fine, just move on down the line.

This is an assembly line. We got to move on down the assembly line, and the, the great master assembly man puts us together. Amen. Just stick with the assembly line, man. Like it said in the prophecy today, stick with the King. He does want you to be perfect. Perfect is maturity, and the key is to stick with the King, like it said in the prophecy today. Just hang in there, don’t disqualify yourself because you got some faults. Just stick with the assembly line, the master craftsman will get the parts and get everything in you as you do. Now that was good. Amen. Remember, the saints are patient, and their trust is in Jesus to do what he said.

chunks.section_question: What makes the second beast different from the first? (Revelation 13:12–15)
chunks.short_answer: He says the second beast causes people to keep worshiping the first beast, and that “he deceives by great wonders,” “brings down fire from heaven,” and has an idol made of the first beast. He says “he gives life to that idol” and “causes that idol to speak,” and notes the Bible says “an idol is nothing” and those who follow idols “become just like them.”
chunks.text:
So this guy has all the power of the first beast to speak, but he causes, and he causes people to worship the first beast. Well, the first, the people are already worshiping the first beast, and this guy pops up and says, continue worshiping the first beast. And the people who worshiped the first beast also worshiped what? Satan. So he says, continue on as you are. So what makes the second beast different from the first beast? Well, he deceives by great wonders. He brings down fire from heaven. He has an idol made of the first beast. He gives life to that idol. He causes that idol to speak. Now that’ll get your attention.

Pretend this is an image of Mary or Buddha or whatever you want it to be. The Bible says an idol is nothing. It has eyes but it can’t see, it has ears it can’t hear. It says it’s powerless, and that’s the fact. People who follow them, the Bible says, become just like them. They can’t see, they can’t hear. Okay, but this guy makes this beast come to life, this, this idol. Now I’m sorry, the idol is living, and not only living, this idol now speaks. Now, how, you know, that would get your attention. I’m surprised that they haven’t come up with the theory of building an idol over in Palestine yet, not just a temple. You guys missed that.

He performs great signs, so that he even makes fire come down from heaven on the earth in the sight of men. chunks.section_question: Why does he say the three-and-a-half-year charts are a problem?
chunks.short_answer: He says the second beast rises after the first beast’s three and a half years with the same power, so “we really got a problem here” fitting three and a half years into “our little charts.” He says “stick with the Bible,” that “everyone that has predicted this stuff has failed so far,” and tells of the Y2K scare, saying “nothing happened.”
chunks.text:
It doesn’t say this beast is around for three and a half years. After the three and a half years period is over, here we got another beast rising with the same power, the first beast who lasted for three and a half years. We really got a problem here. Do you see the problem, trying to make three and a half years work into our little charts? Hallelujah. Church, don’t get wrapped up in that nonsense. Stick with the Bible. Everyone that has predicted this stuff has failed so far, and it’s been going on for almost 2,000 years. Every millennium, everybody thought the second coming was here, and the last one they thought the second coming was here. My church asked me to teach on the Y2K problem and the end time. You know, we’re supposed to, everything was supposed to shut down and cars crash because lights don’t work anymore, and we get flooded because the gates of the dams don’t work anymore, and all the, man, and Christians went out and bought into that, and they bought storage food and light, uh, uh, flashlights and all this stuff, and I go, “Folks, it ain’t going to happen.”

I had two things going for me: I knew the scriptures, and I used to work in the computers. I know a computer does nothing. Nothing comes out except what you put into it. And so my scientific knowledge with my Bible knowledge just confirmed that nothing’s going to happen, and guess what? Nothing happened. Now, in third world countries when I went preaching, and I told them Jesus wasn’t coming in the year 2000, and wasn’t going to come for 13 or more years after the year 2000, they got mad at me. See, we want him to come so desperately, we want him to fit into our agenda. Let, let me give you a theory. You ready for a theory? A Kincer wild imagination theory. I mean, everybody else is throwing them out. Three and a half years.

chunks.section_question: Does he say it could be 1,000 years before Jesus returns? (2 Peter 3:8)
chunks.short_answer: He offers what he calls a “wild imagination theory”: “suppose that 1,000 years from now the world is still going on and Jesus hasn’t come,” since “a thousand years is as a day.” He says “the Bible plainly says nobody” knows when, and asks, “are we going to quit fantasizing and start living in the present generation.”
chunks.text: Suppose that 1,000 years from now the world is still going on and Jesus hasn’t come. Have you got that? A thousand years is as a day, and a day is as a thousand years. Now what are the theory people going to be preaching 1,000 years from now? These three and a half years is a thousand years, is a day, we’re at the 3,000th year, just 50 more years and it’s going to happen. And the Bible plainly says nobody what? Knows when. Are we going to quit fantasizing and start living in the present generation and be who we are supposed to be and identify what’s going on in our time? Amen. Now that was a good preaching.

First six. They will not worship God on the seventh day, God rested. They don’t go to church, they don’t believe in God. Second six.

chunks.section_question: When did the last days begin, and can we know when Jesus returns?
chunks.short_answer: He says “we’re not allowed to add to the word,” and that “shortly” in Revelation 1 and 22:6 was true “since Christ ascended.” He says the last days began at Pentecost, so “we have been living in the last days for 2,000 years” and may be for “another thousand,” and that people said Christ was coming in 1960 and later years. He says we can know “what’s happening in our generation,” like the virgins who were “awake and ready.”
chunks.text:
He says, “He who has wisdom.” I tell you, I don’t have it. I can’t, all the wisdom I got from the scriptures, and I can’t find it revealed anywhere. Have you? And we’re not allowed to add to the word, so we can’t make up our own definition of this thing. Hallelujah. chunks.section_question: How does Satan disguise himself as an angel of light? (2 Corinthians 11:14–15)
chunks.short_answer: He says “Satan himself is transformed into an angel of light,” and that those who follow him “come at you like their ideal is good.” He gives atheists, humanists and freethinkers as people “disguised as angels of righteousness” who say “they’re lying to you, they’re deceiving you, we got the truth.” He ends the virgins illustration with “I’m awake, I know what’s happening.”
chunks.text: Not the one that ran out of oil, not the ones that had oil, been the ones that said, “Come on, man, I’m awake, I know what’s happening.” Satan himself is transformed into an angel of light. “Therefore it is no great thing if his ministers also be transformed as the ministers of righteousness.” Scripture, right? Supernatural. We’re going to show you supernatural. This beast works supernaturally, got it? Satan, you know, they don’t come at you as, as evil, they come at you like their ideal is good. Don’t atheists believe they are right? Don’t they tell everybody like they really know what’s right? And the humanist, the freethinker, yeah. See, they’re disguised as angels of righteousness, of right. They’re not going to come out and say, “I’m lying to you, man.” No. They’re going to be saying that church, man, they’re lying to you, they’re deceiving you, we got the truth.

chunks.section_question: Should we follow signs and wonders? (Deuteronomy 13:1–3)
chunks.short_answer: He reads that if a prophet gives “a sign, a wonder” and says “let’s go after and serve other gods,” “you shall not listen to them.” He says he went to a revival in Lakeland, Florida, and “it was the biggest gimmick I ever seen in my life” because “they were focusing on miracles that weren’t happening.” This is his opinion and has not been verified here.
chunks.text: Okay. Now, “If there arise among you a prophet that gives you a sign, a wonder,” an amazing thing, a supernatural act, “and then they say, let’s go after and serve other gods, you shall not listen to them.” Now, why were people running down to Lakeland, Florida, for this revival thing that was supposed to happen, and the pastors here in [unclear] were seeking God for the same visitation that was in Lakeland, Florida? I went down there, and it was the biggest gimmick I ever seen in my life. And what was the gimmick? They were focusing on miracles that weren’t happening. Nothing was happening, and they were saying it happened, much less if they can make one or two happen. Are you out there, church?

paragraphs.text: Okay. scriptures.text_nkjv: “If there arises among you a prophet or a dreamer of dreams, and he gives you a sign or a wonder, and the sign or the wonder comes to pass, of which he spoke to you, saying, ‘Let us go after other gods’—which you have not known—‘and let us serve them,’ you shall not listen to the words of that prophet or that dreamer of dreams, for the LORD your God is testing you to know whether you love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul.

chunks.section_question: What power did the sorcerers of Egypt really have? (Exodus 7–8)
chunks.short_answer: He says the sorcerers “never had any power till Moses showed up,” and then God gave them “limited authority, limited supernatural power.” They could copy a sign but not undo it, because “they can’t do any more than God lets them do,” and “the sorcerers could not create life.”
chunks.text:
“The sorcerers of Egypt also did like manner with their enchantments, but could not make lice,” saying, “This is the finger of God.” You see, the sorcerers of Egypt never had any power till Moses showed up. They weren’t down there turning water to blood, they weren’t down there turning their rod to a snake, they weren’t down there bringing frogs out of the river. When Moses showed up, God gave them limited authority, limited supernatural power. And so when Pharaoh said, “Okay, magicians, sorcerers, you change your rod into a snake,” well, they didn’t need any more snakes, they needed to change Moses’s snake back to a rod. So they threw down their rod and it turned to a snake, and guess what? Moses ate them all. They didn’t have any rod to turn back. Are you there? See, they had limited supernatural power. When Moses poured the water out and it became blood, Pharaoh said, “Okay, you sorcerers, do that.” So they poured water out, became blood. They didn’t need any more blood, they needed the water, the blood changed back to water.

See, God gave them limited supernatural power. What they really needed was to overpower Moses and turn the blood back to water. This is what you got to remember. And then Moses brought up frogs, and Pharaoh said, “Okay, sorcerers, bring up...” Well, they don’t want any more frogs. Frogs! So the sorcerers put out their staff, and here comes more frogs. The thing, they didn’t need more frogs, they needed the other frogs removed, but they couldn’t do it. Why? They can’t do any more than God lets them do. And God says, “Okay, you want more frogs? Okay, we’ll give you more frogs. You think there’s power in your sorcery? Go ahead.” But when they came to the [unclear], where they created something out of nothing, God says, “This is as far as you go,” and the sorcerers could not create life.

Now the magicians so worked with their enchantments to bring forth lice, but they could not. So there were lice on man and beast. Then the magicians said to Pharaoh, “This is the finger of God.” But Pharaoh’s heart grew hard, and he did not heed them, just as the LORD had said.

chunks.short_answer: He says the idol that comes to life “has got to be a ventriloquist somewhere,” and that the sorcerers had “supernatural power to deceive people.” Citing Acts 16:16, he says the girl with a spirit of divination “had limited supernatural ability,” and that he knew a person at a revival who told people their addresses “had a familiar spirit.” He asks whether people “just fall for every little prophetic word of knowledge.” This is his account and has not been verified here.

And that’s why this idol that comes to life has got to be a ventriloquist somewhere, just throwing things out. Hallelujah. Isn’t this wonderful? Isn’t this book great? They have limited power, but they did have supernatural power to deceive people. chunks.section_question: Who was Simon the sorcerer, and what is the end goal? (Acts 8:9)
chunks.short_answer: Reading that Simon “used sorcery and bewitched the people of Samaria,” he says the people said he was the power of God, and the power of sorcery “comes from the kingdom of darkness.” He says “just because someone can do some kind of supernatural thing, and it’s limited, you don’t fall for it,” and asks, “what’s their message? What’s their end goal?”
chunks.text: Hallelujah. Simon, in Acts 8:9, “used sorcery and bewitched the people of Samaria, giving out that himself was some great one, to whom they all,” how many? All “gave heed, from the least to the greatest, saying, This man is the power of” Satan? No. Who do they say he was? “The power of God.” And who does the scripture say this power of sorcery comes from? The kingdom of darkness, church. Are you there? See, just because someone can do some kind of supernatural thing, and it’s limited, you don’t fall for it. What’s their message? What’s their end goal? And in Lakeland, Florida, they had their end goal as some woman angel. Nowhere in the Bible is there a woman angel. In fact, angels don’t have sex, they’re just spirits. They don’t have a penis, they don’t have a vagina, they’re just spirits. What I mean, he uses “he” so we can understand. Ain’t that right?

scriptures.text_nkjv: But there was a certain man called Simon, who previously practiced sorcery in the city and astonished the people of Samaria, claiming that he was someone great, to whom they all gave heed, from the least to the greatest, saying, “This man is the great power of God.” And they heeded him because he had astonished them with his sorceries for a long time.

faqs.question: Who does he say will not worship the beast?
faqs.answer: He says “those in the Book of Life” won’t worship, and “all the earth worships” except “the ones written in the Book of Life, the ones that got born again.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: All who dwell on the earth will worship him, whose names have not been written in the Book of Life of the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world.

faqs.question: Does he say joining a church makes you saved?
faqs.answer: He says “churches just put people on the roll book, they just want attendance,” but “Jesus said you got to be born again of the word and the Spirit.” He asks, “how are they going to get birthed in the word if we don’t preach the word?”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Jesus answered, “Most assuredly, I say to you, unless one is born of water and the Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of God.

faqs.question: What does he say “the patience and the faith of the saints” is?
faqs.answer: He says “they’re going to stick with Jesus no matter what,” and that “they are patiently waiting for Jesus to fulfill his word in them and in the world.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Here is the patience of the saints; here are those who keep the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus.

faqs.question: Does he say Christians will be raptured out of difficulty?
faqs.answer: He says no: “they’re still here,” and “we don’t have to get raptured out.” He says “Jesus is big enough to keep us in any kind of difficulty of this world.”

faqs.question: What does he say the word “Christian” means?
faqs.answer: He says “Christian means I came from Christ, I follow Christ, I act like Christ,” and “there’s a big difference between a believer and a Christian.”

faqs.question: What does he mean by the “assembly line”?
faqs.answer: He says “we got to move on down the assembly line,” and “the great master assembly man puts us together.” He says “don’t disqualify yourself because you got some faults,” because “the master craftsman will get the parts and get everything in you.”

faqs.question: What does he say the Bible says about idols?
faqs.answer: He says “an idol is nothing. It has eyes but it can’t see, it has ears it can’t hear,” and that “people who follow them … become just like them.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Their idols are silver and gold, The work of men’s hands. They have mouths, but they do not speak; Eyes they have, but they do not see; They have ears, but they do not hear; Noses they have, but they do not smell; They have hands, but they do not handle; Feet they have, but they do not walk; Nor do they mutter through their throat. Those who make them are like them; So is everyone who trusts in them.

faqs.question: Does he say end-time predictions have been reliable?
faqs.answer: He says no: “Church, don’t get wrapped up in that nonsense. Stick with the Bible. Everyone that has predicted this stuff has failed so far.”

faqs.question: What does he say about the Y2K scare?
faqs.answer: He says he told people “it ain’t going to happen,” because “a computer does nothing” except what is put into it. His “scientific knowledge with my Bible knowledge just confirmed that nothing’s going to happen, and guess what? Nothing happened.”

faqs.question: When does he say the last days started?
faqs.answer: He says “day of Pentecost, when he poured out his Spirit on all flesh,” and “we have been living in the last days for 2,000 years.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: ‘And it shall come to pass in the last days, says God, That I will pour out of My Spirit on all flesh; Your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, Your young men shall see visions, Your old men shall dream dreams.

faqs.question: Does he say we can know when Jesus is coming back?
faqs.answer: He says no: “no one” knows. He recalls that “they said he was coming in 1960, 1962” and later, and says “our generations might be here another thousand years from now.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: “But of that day and hour no one knows, not even the angels of heaven, but My Father only.

faqs.question: What does he say the sorcerers of Egypt really needed to do?
faqs.answer: He says “what they really needed was to overpower Moses and turn the blood back to water,” but they could not, because God gave them only “limited supernatural power.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Now the magicians so worked with their enchantments to bring forth lice, but they could not. So there were lice on man and beast. Then the magicians said to Pharaoh, “This is the finger of God.” But Pharaoh’s heart grew hard, and he did not heed them, just as the LORD had said.

faqs.question: What does he say about someone telling people their addresses?
faqs.answer: He says “you can find where I live in the phone book,” and “I need a source of power to live in this life for Christ and do what’s right.” He says “limited knowledge” like that “doesn’t fool those that are written in the Lamb’s Book of Life.” This is his account.

faqs.question: What does he say about vague prophetic words?
faqs.answer: He says “tell me exactly what you see,” not general words about cars and rivers. He says “us Spirit-filled people have got to get the program,” because “we’re one of the worst for this nonsense.”
